title: Should women train like men?
summary: Prompted by Curlean-X's critique of Athlean-X's women's programs, NH argues women should follow the same core principles as men (strength training, compounds, progressive overload) but apply volume, intensity and body-part emphasis differently. Most women want lower body development, respond poorly in shoulders and traps, and can't look like men naturally.
claims: The fitness industry is predatory toward everyone, especially women
YouTube fitness is made for men; women rarely get efforts tailored to their needs
Men are stronger on average and the strongest humans will always be men
Women's programs of kickbacks and band work promising big gains are lies copied from crash-diet marketing
Strength training is essential for men and women alike; he can't think of a movement pattern women shouldn't do
Women who start real strength training get very strong; he saw women go from one to two plate squats without ballooning in weight
Women dominate ultra-long-distance swimming thanks to oxygen distribution and buoyancy
Women may recover better from wear and tear, show more knee valgus but possibly fewer knee injuries
Women can rep weights very close to their 1RM, which breaks standard RPE calculations
Volume and intensity may need different application for women
Most women want bigger lower bodies, toned arms and abs, so a pressing-and-curls man's program doesn't fit their goals
Women have far less upper body muscle and fewer androgen receptors there; blasting their shoulders and traps wastes volume better spent on legs
Even women wanting a bigger upper body shouldn't get an upper-dominant split
Telling women to just train like men is virtue signaling or laziness; women-specific programming needs developing, mostly by women
Women can't look like men naturally; lifting won't make them bulky
Big round shoulders and huge traps on women are dead giveaways of PEDs
Women have good potential for biceps, mid-back and rear delts, okay triceps, and are mostly non-responders in shoulders and upper traps
Women should follow core principles of volume and intensity manipulation, compounds and progressive overload, but apply them differently
Pull-ups are extremely hard for women given their lower-body mass distribution; he has seen one woman do one
